title: Shapla Chattar Crackdown
subtitle: Security forces cleared a Hefazat-e-Islam rally in Motijheel amid the wider 2013 war-crimes-trial crisis.
summary: On 5-6 May 2013, security forces cleared Hefazat-e-Islam supporters from Shapla Chattar in Motijheel, Dhaka. The episode followed months of polarization around war-crimes trials, Shahbag mobilization, and Islamist counter-mobilization.
heroTagline: A night-time operation became one of the most disputed episodes of 2013.
whyItMatters: The crackdown matters because it linked accountability politics, religious mobilization, state force, and contested casualty narratives in one volatile episode of contemporary Bangladesh.
longTermLegacy: Its legacy remains tied to debates over protest policing, religious-party mobilization, accountability trials, and the reliability of competing casualty claims.
identityMemoryNotes: For supporters, critics, and rights groups, Shapla Chattar became a shorthand for unresolved arguments about state violence and political legitimacy.
